      <title>Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision</link>
      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections</link>
      <description><p>Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result</p><p>The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.</p><p>Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/04/anc-south-africa-local-elections-water-outages-power-cuts">voters turning away from the party</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Violent storms lash northern Iraq and parts of Iran, while Portugal faces strong winds and Japan braces for further snowfall</p><p>Deadly flash floods hit northern Iraq on Saturday as severe thunderstorms swept across the region, including in neighbouring Iran.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/09/pope-leo-argentina-visit-speech-javier-milei-austerity</link>
      <description><p>Pontiff tells Argentina’s president the economy must benefit all on second stop of 12-day Latin America tour</p><p>Pope Leo XIV has delivered a stinging critique of Argentine president Javier Milei’s harsh austerity measures, insisting growth must benefit all in a speech met with rapturous applause in Buenos Aires.</p><p>“The economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy,” he said on Sunday, shortly after landing in Argentina on the second leg of a Latin America tour.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/09/pope-leo-argentina-visit-speech-javier-milei-austerity">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>President has opposing views on many issues, and once called Leo’s predecessor the ‘representative of the Evil One’</p><p>Trees are being planted in the garden.       <description><p>Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event</p><p>Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event.</p><p>High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body.       <title>US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/10/china-green-energy-john-kerry-cop31</link>
      <description><p>Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/live/2026/nov/10/cop31-live-fossil-fuel-carbon-emissions-climate-crisis-latest-news-updates">Cop31 live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>China is leading the world <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/feb/05/china-green-energy-sector-investment-growth">in moving away from fossil fuels</a>, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.</p><p>As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/10/china-green-energy-john-kerry-cop31">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/10/australia-manadatory-reporting-openai-medicare-hack</link>
      <description><p>Government flags criminal law changes to ensure companies can’t argue in future ‘that someone didn’t know the computer was loaded’</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily political email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>OpenAI will not face criminal penalties over <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/media/2026/oct/06/openai-australia-parliament-inquiry-jason-kwon">the Medicare data breach</a>, but the prime minister has flagged changes to Australia’s criminal law to crack down on future breaches by artificial intelligence companies.</p><p>Anthony Albanese on Tuesday released the recommendations of a “rapid review” into the June breach of a Medicare statistics reporting service portal administered by Services Australia, but not the findings or the report itself, which he committed to releasing in the future.</p><p>Maintaining security controls across all stages of development and deployment.</p><p>Identifying and managing serious risks associated with their models.</p><p>Providing mandatory notification of incidents to the Australian government rapidly.</p><p>Allowing independent evaluation of their models.</p><p>Maintaining and publishing safety and security frameworks to ensure good governance, risk management and transparency.</p><p>Responding to updated standards and rules as technologies change.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/10/australia-manadatory-reporting-openai-medicare-hack">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>US-led talks in Abu Dhabi break up after four hours but are expected to resume tomorrow as Zelenskyy says humanitarian issues were discussed</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/10/us-officials-russia-ukraine-war-abu-dhabi-talks">US officials seek ‘final end’ to Russia-Ukraine war as talks begin</a></p></li></ul><p>The EU has said it stands ready “to come with a swift and united response” after France blamed Iran for a spate of cyber-attacks on supermarket freezers and chillers that caused millions of euros of damage.</p><p>Speaking to journalists on Monday, French foreign minister <strong>Jean-Noël Barrot</strong> said “<strong>Europe-wide sanctions</strong>” would be imposed against those responsible as he announced <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/09/france-blames-irans-revolutionary-guards-for-cyber-attacks-on-supermarket-fridges">France believed that Iran’s Revolutionary Guards were “responsible for this attack”</a>.</p><p><em>We acknowledge that France has attributed these (cyber-attacks) to Iran. Pending discussions with member states, we as (the) European Union, <strong>we stand ready to come with a swift and united response</strong>.</em></p><p><em>We as the EU, <strong>we have consistently called on all states to refrain from malicious behaviour in the cyberspace</strong>. And we will continue to address such malicious behavior, making use of all the tools that we have also under the EU cyber diplomacy toolbox, including sanctions.</em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/10/ukraine-russia-war-us-talks-abu-dhabi-europe-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>en</language><title>The economic issues and policy in France - RFI</title><description>Follow any political information, cultural, sporting and live streaming on RFI. The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:13:02 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French student protests continue amid deadlock over education reforms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-student-protests-continue-amid-deadlock-over-education-reforms</link><description>
Students and teachers are planning a new day of strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday, as talks with the government remain deadlocked, nearly two months after the start of protests by high school and university students.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37288fa8-dcd4-11f1-aace-7ff548d44c0a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 06:59:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner joins race for French presidency</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-olympic-judo-champion-teddy-riner-joins-race-for-french-presidency</link><description>
France's five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's presidential election, expressing concern particularly over "the rise of the far right".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff9ac7be-dc3c-11f1-a6ee-d528d7ed3f40</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:44:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg">© AP - Michel Euler</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM's move to increase minimum wage fails to convince unions</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-pm-s-move-to-increase-minimum-wage-fails-to-convince-unions</link><description>
The French government on Monday announced a 1.6 percent increase in the national minimum wage, alongside a series of measures aimed at easing cost of living pressures. However, the decision fell well short of the demands of trade unions, who have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1fb23d3e-dc42-11f1-9f6d-714e057b766f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:36:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg">© Emma Da Silva/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'I still have nightmares': victim of police violence seeks justice six years on</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-i-still-have-nightmares-victim-of-police-violence-seeks-justice-six-years-on-michel-zecler</link><description>
Three French police officers are due to go on trial on Monday over the brutal beating of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020 – a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police violence and racism.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0aa97116-dc27-11f1-890c-17b2c492ee48</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 14:29:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/88ce45b6-dba1-11f1-91d2-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/FRANCE-JUSTICE-MICHEL-ZECLER.jpg">AFP - JOEL SAGET</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mélenchon bets on radical change as French presidential race takes shape</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-m%C3%A9lenchon-bets-on-radical-change-as-french-presidential-race-takes-shape</link><description>
Leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to pursue an uncompromising programme of radical change, as he bids for the French presidency in 2027 – despite warnings that his divisive politics could ultimately hand victory to far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">273d195c-dc1a-11f1-8d60-5f29074843e0</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:01:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28b90688-dc1f-11f1-84be-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/M%C3%A9lenchon-7-November-2026.jpg">©  KENZO TRIBOUILLARD / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French food bank donations fall as frequency of use spikes in cost of living crisis</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-drop-in-french-food-bank-collection-as-rising-cost-of-living-hits-donations</link><description>
France’s annual food bank collection has gathered less than expected in the face of the rising cost of living, which has left people with less to spend on donations. The three-day campaign, which ended on Sunday, aimed to collect enough food to provide the equivalent of 20 million meals.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7b3dffa-dc2b-11f1-8a7f-0f7ff0c2412a</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:09:22 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b1392996-dbc2-11f1-af3e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32TL9GD-1.jpg">© Mehdi Fedouach/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French MPs weigh up debate on right-wing TV channel ban as petition tops 1m</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-mps-to-weigh-debate-on-banning-conservative-tv-channel-as-petition-tops-1m-cnews</link><description>
A petition calling for French television channel CNews, often compared to American broadcaster Fox News, to be shut down has received more than a million signatures, two days before lawmakers meet to consider whether a ban should be debated in parliament.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19210fc8-dc0a-11f1-bd4e-25468b64d7d5</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 06:52:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/b0dc3b9c-dba8-11f1-b566-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D66Z6FA.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Unions vow to maintain pressure on government after fourth wave of protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261108-unions-vow-to-keep-pressure-on-french-government-after-fourth-wave-of-protests</link><description>
Education union chiefs on Sunday vowed to maintain pressure on the French government after student organisations called for another day of nationwide strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">36cb7bb6-dac6-11f1-b148-e9346ba72bac</guid><pubDate>Sun, 08 Nov 2026 11:00:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a57fc52e-db63-11f1-b306-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/prote.jpg">AP Photo/Emma Da Silva - Emma Da Silva</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>French students vow to continue protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/video/20261107-french-students-vow-to-continue-protests-paris</link><description>
French pupils and students are protesting and blockading schools over poor conditions and a university admissions system (Parcoursup) seen as over-selective and opaque. Despite recent concessions by the government, students at Hélène Boucher high school in Paris say they'll continue, even after riot place were sent to break their blockade.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed31678-c945-11f1-84f0-638c1c1f5fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-16T075646Z-1864054812-RC274OA7GQ58-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST-2.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8c9b5ff0-dab9-11f1-a45a-31b57fcb4ae5</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 15:02:47 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France braces for second day of protests within 48 hours</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261107-france-braces-for-second-day-of-protests-within-48-hours</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people were expected to take to the streets on Saturday for a day of protests over the poor conditions in schools and the rising cost of living.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">33ad1cbc-da96-11f1-8df4-1da1eb33321e</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 12:10:04 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb2ec67e-d9cd-11f1-a5cc-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T151241Z-1266580735-RC2OHOAVSIEZ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Hannah McKay</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: France's student protests and how they fuelled a larger social movement</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261106-podcast-france-s-student-protests-and-how-they-fuelled-a-larger-social-movement-may-68</link><description>
A look at France's high school protests and how they have fed into an ongoing social movement. What are the students protesting against? What impact has the police crackdown had? How has the government reacted? And a comparison with student movements of the past.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/884fdc42-d9cd-11f1-80bf-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-152-peach-pink.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bcd965aa-d9cd-11f1-b272-af07f9a85ea6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:29:10 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French lawyers to sue interior minister over 'mutilation' of young protesters</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-french-lawyers-to-sue-interior-minister-over-mutilation-of-young-protesters</link><description>
Lawyers representing at least 18 people injured during protests in France in recent weeks say they intend to file a complaint against Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez over his alleged responsibility for police brutality.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dba18ef0-d9e5-11f1-863b-f351e1b5079d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 14:39:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ad744280-bea5-11f1-8056-578a4b968fd6/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-02T104258Z-1424347954-RC2XUNAITHZX-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nacho Doce</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'AI cannot do everything': bullying experts warn against confiding in chatbots</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-one-quarter-of-young-bullying-victims-turning-to-ai-for-help-study-finds</link><description>
As a growing number of victims turn to artificial intelligence for help, experts warn that, while a virtual confidante can offer temporary relief, the focus must be on prevention and support.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">71185a8c-d797-11f1-a35f-45b5729425b2</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:35:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/808c3c9c-cd36-11f1-b7ef-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/yamu-jay-school-bullying-9060270.jpg">© pixabay / Yamu_Jay</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Latest figures show domestic violence still major problem in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261106-chilling-figures-show-domestic-violence-still-major-problem-in-france</link><description>
French authorities recorded 285,000 victims of domestic violence in 2025, mostly women, representing a 5 percent increase in a year. It comes as lawmakers debate a new law against sexual and gender-based violence that is due to be finalised at the beginning of 2027.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">77dc943a-d92e-11f1-90a5-5193511bd582</guid><pubDate>Fri, 06 Nov 2026 06:08:15 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb36a16c-43a7-11f1-8f1d-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26090564561960.jpg">© Andreea Alexandru / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>‘We’ll get them’: Macron’s private comments on rivals revealed in new book</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-we-ll-get-them-macron-s-private-comments-on-rivals-revealed-in-new-book</link><description>
Private messages exchanged between French President Emmanuel Macron and journalist Françoise Degois over two years have been published in a new book, revealing his views on political rivals, the rise of the far right and his own leadership. The president reportedly learnt of the book’s existence just three days before its release.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ed7d8d46-d8f9-11f1-8648-c35846abfa7a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:07:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/fb95d9d2-d896-11f1-b8ef-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP22177506677032-1.jpg">© AP - Susan Walsh </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French prosecutors investigate €100m cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel banking group</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-prosecutors-investigate-%E2%82%AC100m-cyberattack-on-cr%C3%A9dit-mutuel-banking-group</link><description>
French prosecutors have opened an investigation into a sophisticated cyberattack on Crédit Mutuel Arkéa involving fraudulent transfers estimated at around €100 million, as the Brittany-based banking group races to recover the stolen funds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d4c86e50-d8f5-11f1-8292-031c66ea2070</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 12:31:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a8dda14a-d907-11f1-a6f6-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/Cr%C3%A9dit-Mutuel-Ark%C3%A9a.jpg">AFP - FRED TANNEAU</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>MPs unanimously reject 2027 French budget as political deadlock continues</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-mps-unanimously-reject-2027-budget-as-political-deadlock-deepens</link><description>
France's National Assembly has overwhelmingly rejected the government's draft budget for 2027 after MPs from across the political spectrum voted against a heavily amended version of the legislation, sending the bill to the Senate in its original form and setting the stage for another round of difficult negotiations.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">94610092-d8ec-11f1-83cc-05d8d1a87801</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:19:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8c795750-c2d3-11f1-9d03-c55799ef8309/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D2DV9WP.jpg">© AFP/Dimitar Dilkoff</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mass protests sweep France as workers and students demand higher pay and funding</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261105-french-unions-join-forces-for-nationwide-strike-as-protests-intensify</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Thursday as workers, students and pensioners joined nationwide strikes and demonstrations demanding higher wages, action on the cost of living and better public services. Nearly 1.6 million people joined the marches, including 350,000 in Paris, the CGT union said. The Interior Ministry gave a much lower nationwide estimate of around 600,000.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d1ac4db2-d847-11f1-8e8e-b39696b484d3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 05 Nov 2026 07:11:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e9309cc-d936-11f1-b338-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26309546527183.jpg">© AP Photo/Thibault Camus</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students blockade dozens of high schools in France before nationwide strike</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261103-students-blockade-dozens-of-high-schools-in-france-before-nationwide-strike</link><description>
Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike later this week.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f797ebc-d75d-11f1-9716-917a4357a158</guid><pubDate>Tue, 03 Nov 2026 12:20:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/21c9ae56-d6d2-11f1-afea-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D64N373.jpg">© Matthieu Rondel / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Calls mount to ban French TV channel following racist killing</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261102-calls-mount-to-ban-french-tv-channel-after-racist-killing</link><description>
A petition urging that a French television channel be taken off air gained traction on Monday, after accusations that far-right views it aired contributed to the racist killing of a black man. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7c5b8-d6c6-11f1-947b-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4Y89JC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7c5b8-d6c6-11f1-947b-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4Y89JC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8d41d30a-d6d4-11f1-996a-c9565a8083a3</guid><pubDate>Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:54:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/25b7c5b8-d6c6-11f1-947b-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D4Y89JC.jpg">AFP - SIMON WOHLFAHRT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France braces for fresh protests as students to resume school blockades</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261102-france-braces-for-fresh-protests-as-students-to-resume-school-blockades</link><description>
France is readying for another week of protests after the head of a student group said a campaign of high school blockades would restart Monday, ahead of a nationwide day of strikes and protests on Thursday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bf6d858-c15b-11f1-967e-b942c38e4bd7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-06T073959Z-1661401214-RC2JXNALODN9-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bf6d858-c15b-11f1-967e-b942c38e4bd7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-06T073959Z-1661401214-RC2JXNALODN9-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fe830974-d5e6-11f1-94c2-0ddebd68042b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 02 Nov 2026 07:09:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bf6d858-c15b-11f1-967e-b942c38e4bd7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-06T073959Z-1661401214-RC2JXNALODN9-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Tom Nicholson</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Five British anti-immigration activists arrested in northern France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261101-five-british-anti-migrant-ultra-right-activists-arrested-in-north-of-france</link><description>
French police say they've arrested five British far-right activists found carrying tear gas bombs, as they were filming themselves harassing migrants near the northern Channel port of Dunkirk.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/31d0c036-4bf0-11ec-abc5-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP21324042369756.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/31d0c036-4bf0-11ec-abc5-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP21324042369756.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ed941388-d5fa-11f1-9c92-8d270bd12c5c</guid><pubDate>Sun, 01 Nov 2026 14:18:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/31d0c036-4bf0-11ec-abc5-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP21324042369756.jpg">© AP Photo/Louis Witter</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attack on police</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261101-france-launches-attempted-murder-probe-after-petrol-bomb-attack-on-police</link><description>
France has launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f2d8ffc4-d565-11f1-aa94-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/84b0f9d200b86233f18834393d966b98a1b52af4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f2d8ffc4-d565-11f1-aa94-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/84b0f9d200b86233f18834393d966b98a1b52af4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c8e54780-d5f7-11f1-8f9a-d78b8e884648</guid><pubDate>Sun, 01 Nov 2026 13:26:02 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/f2d8ffc4-d565-11f1-aa94-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/84b0f9d200b86233f18834393d966b98a1b52af4.jpg">© Sameer AL-DOUMY / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France sees third weekend of protests as youth-led rallies sweep Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261031-france-sees-third-weekend-of-protests-as-youth-led-rallies-sweep-europe</link><description>
Hundreds of thousands of mostly young protesters, some dressed as clowns and witches for Halloween, took to the streets across France on Saturday in a third weekend of demonstrations over living costs and education. Police fired tear gas in Paris after clashes broke out at the end of the march. Youth rallies were also held in Germany and Italy.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/316d67d0-d54c-11f1-a9e9-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T161057Z-1540280500-RC2FEOAN304W-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/316d67d0-d54c-11f1-a9e9-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T161057Z-1540280500-RC2FEOAN304W-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1eff833e-d543-11f1-b06a-ffc2e7fd2caa</guid><pubDate>Sat, 31 Oct 2026 17:46:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/316d67d0-d54c-11f1-a9e9-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T161057Z-1540280500-RC2FEOAN304W-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Manon Cruz</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Minister warns of risk of violence ahead of Halloween 'night of darkness' protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261031-minister-warns-of-risk-of-violence-ahead-of-halloween-night-of-darkness-protests</link><description>
With student groups and Yellow Vest activists set for a third consecutive weekend of demonstrations against poor conditions in schools and the rising cost of living, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has said 70,000 police officers and gendarmes will be deployed across France on Saturday. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/69f81ba6-d450-11f1-b62e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3KU3H6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/69f81ba6-d450-11f1-b62e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3KU3H6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4b9a3b5e-d445-11f1-9e6a-5f14884e5daf</guid><pubDate>Sat, 31 Oct 2026 08:34:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/69f81ba6-d450-11f1-b62e-bf1914cabd52/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3KU3H6.jpg">AFP - CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <title>Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2026/nov/10/ultimate-1-50-the-male-footballers-best-associated-with-each-squad-number</link>
      <description><p>Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? Here’s our list and the stories behind it</p><p>The relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50. Various factors were taken into consideration, including how long a player wore/has worn that number, what they achieved/have achieved in it, why they decided to wear it in the first place and, in some cases, how distinctly it has become associated with them in death. The below list is highly subjective and ultimately a bit of fun, but don’t let that stop you being shocked and furious in equal measure.</p><p>***</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2026/nov/10/ultimate-1-50-the-male-footballers-best-associated-with-each-squad-number">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Celebrations linked to ultra-conservative Christian group</p></li><li><p>‘Our message is of love’ Nmecha says in reply to criticism</p></li></ul><p>Borussia Dortmund and Germany midfielder Felix Nmecha has responded to criticism of goal celebrations linked to an evangelical network by saying they’ve been misunderstood and are not meant to promote “intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form”.</p><p>Nmecha, a devout Christian, was criticised by the Dortmund official supporters’ group at the weekend for celebrating goals with a gesture signifying the “The King’s Return” campaign linked to Ballers in God (BIG), a network of Christian football players.       <title>Ben White says he has no complaints at boos from England fans over self-imposed exile</title>

      <description><ul><li><p>Arsenal defender was jeered during draw with Uruguay</p></li><li><p>‘Everyone can do whatever they want,’ says White</p></li></ul><p>Ben White has said he has no complaints at being booed by England fans when he ended his international exile during <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/mar/27/england-uruguay-international-friendly-match-report">the 1-1 draw with ­Uruguay</a> this year.</p><p>The Arsenal defender, who has returned to Thomas Tuchel’s squad after missing last month’s camp because of injury, became unpopular with some supporters after leaving the 2022 World Cup in Qatar early for personal reasons.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/manchester-united-city-soulless-content-machines-premier-league</link>
      <description><p>United and City dominate the news cycle with stories so strange and vast they threaten to consume the rest of the league</p><p>In Manchester this weekend it was possible to bookend your Thursday‑to‑Sunday entertainment with two cultural events. First up, a debut screening of the re‑released and uncensored Ken Russell film The Devils at Trafford Odeon. And three days later, three miles down the road, Manchester United versus Aston Villa at Old Trafford.</p><p>As expected, one of these events provided a visceral cinematic experience, a deeply disturbing two-hour public meditation on the meaning of faith, blood, fear, power, ritual and the fetishising of objects, climaxing in an orgiastic crowd scene of depraved but undeniably erotic abandon, all acted out on a set in a state of glorious and performative ruin. And the other one was a film with Oliver Reed in it.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/manchester-united-city-soulless-content-machines-premier-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/10/shirt-numbers-tell-story-football-tactical-evolution</link>
      <description><p>In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2026/nov/10/ultimate-1-50-the-male-footballers-best-associated-with-each-squad-number">Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players</a></p></li></ul><p>Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the <em>enganche</em>, the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque.</p><p>But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/10/shirt-numbers-tell-story-football-tactical-evolution">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Cerebral Josh King plots unusual route into Tuchel’s England plans</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/cerebral-josh-king-plots-unusual-route-into-tuchels-england-plans</link>
      <description><p>Armed with an impressive academic record and experience as a rugby fly-half, the teenager is anything but typical</p><p>Josh King is talking with pride about how his mother, Michelle, a university lecturer, has almost finished her PhD in sickle cell disease. The Fulham attacking midfielder, who is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/06/jude-jobe-bellingham-thomas-tuchel-england-croatia-spain-nations-league">in the England squad</a> for the Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain this week, mentions that his father, Steve, is a lawyer and says he might have liked to follow in his footsteps if it had not worked out for him on the pitch.</p><p>King’s background is not that of a typical footballer. Privately educated at Hampton School in south-west London, he aced his GCSEs, achieving A or A* in his 10 subjects. He went on to study part-time for A-levels in French, maths and psychology, getting grades of A, C and D – pretty impressive, especially when you consider he sat the exams in a hotel suite in Romania in the summer of last year while playing for England at the European Under-19 Championship.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/cerebral-josh-king-plots-unusual-route-into-tuchels-england-plans">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/football-comes-together-spain-honour-jesus-de-miguel-tenerife</link>
      <description><p>Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them</p><p>In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/feb/17/osasuna-ante-budimir-real-madrid-bellingham-la-liga">than anyone in their history</a> stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.”</p><p>With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/03/tenerife-footballer-jesus-de-miguel-hospital-collision">who died after a collision on the pitch</a> five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/football-comes-together-spain-honour-jesus-de-miguel-tenerife">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Felix Nmecha’s faith is forcing Borussia Dortmund into an uncomfortable debate</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/felix-nmecha-faith-borussia-dortmund-debate-bundesliga</link>
      <description><p>Midfielder’s spectacular strikes rescued a frustrating day, only for celebrations to reignite dialogue that has followed him through his career</p><p>It was just what they needed at just the right time. For a tricky first half and beyond, Elversberg had been a stone in Borussia Dortmund’s shoe, the promoted side not just keeping the home team at bay but keeping them honest, nourishing ambitions of their own. “The fatigue was clearly visible,” the sporting director, Ole Book, said to Sky after a week which had <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/31/european-football-harry-kane-bayern-munich-borussia-dortmund-milan-inter-barcelona">contained </a><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/31/european-football-harry-kane-bayern-munich-borussia-dortmund-milan-inter-barcelona">Der Klassiker</a></em> in Munich and a hard-fought Champions League victory against Betis. “We were a bit too focused on managing the game, which was understandable.”</p><p>Enter Felix Nmecha. BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference. It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/felix-nmecha-faith-borussia-dortmund-debate-bundesliga">Continue reading...</a></description>

href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">Saturday defeat</a> to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances.</p><p>In the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/24/aston-villa-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">2-1</a> defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/31/manchester-city-brighton-premier-league-match-report">1-0</a> home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table.</p><p><em>This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/jul/20/sign-up-for-soccer-with-jonathan-wilson-his-free-weekly-newsletter-on-european-soccer?utm_term=68ff7d8f6c73dffc08f382888be1de2a&amp;amp;utm_campaign=SoccerwithJonathanWilson&amp;amp;utm_source=esp&amp;amp;utm_medium=Email&amp;amp;CMP=soccerwithjonathanwilson_email">Subscribe for free here</a>.</em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/manchester-city-enzo-maresca-premier-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/rodrigo-mora-roma-lazio-rome-serie-a</link>
      <description><p>Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a Scudetto</p><p>After nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football.</p><p>The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/03/manchester-united-roma-champions-league-match-report">midweek defeat against Manchester United</a>. That result meant the <em>Giallorossi</em> had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/rodrigo-mora-roma-lazio-rome-serie-a">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>WSL talking points: Tullis-Joyce takes charge and is Shaw the perfect striker?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/wsl-talking-points-khadija-shaw-manchester-city-phallon-tullis-joyce</link>
      <description><p>The City forward hit a WSL hat-trick for the ninth time while Eva Olid’s United have found defensive stability</p><p>Not only did Khadija “Bunny” Shaw score a record-extending ninth WSL hat-trick, she scored a “perfect hat-trick” for the fourth time in the competition, something nobody else has managed more than once. Against West Ham the Jamaica striker opened the scoring with her left foot, headed home her second off the underside of the crossbar and tucked in her third with her right foot late on. It helped her side towards a 5-0 win that opened up a two-point gap at the top of the table and stretched Shaw’s lead in the race to be the top division’s top scorer to a five-goal advantage over her nearest challenger, Océane Hurtré. Can anybody stop her relentless pursuit of another Golden Boot? It would appear not. <strong>Tom Garry</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/liverpool-arsenal-wsl-match-report">Match report: Liverpool 1-2 Arsenal</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/wsl-talking-points-khadija-shaw-manchester-city-phallon-tullis-joyce">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>US inflation rose 0.4% in October as price increases cooled and gas costs dipped</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/october-inflation-report</link>
      <description><p>New data comes after Republicans’ midterms losses – which were largely seen as a rebuke of the party over high prices</p><p>US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, slightly above expectations but still a cooldown in price increases as the cost of gas dipped during the month.</p><p>The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not release the usual year-over-year inflation figure as part of the consumer price index (CPI), which measures the price of a basket of goods and services, as data was not collected in October 2025 during the government shutdown.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/10/october-inflation-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/10/nvidia-shareholder-lawsuit-jensen-huang-relationship-suspected-chinese-spy-fbi-trump-bank-of-england-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/09/trump-iran-war">Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over”</a>.</p><p>Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”.       <description><p>‘Low-hire, low-fire’ labor market shows sluggish growth but few layoffs, with an interest rate hike expected in December</p><p>The US added 165,000 jobs to the economy in October, a sign of resilience in the labor market amid war in the Middle East and inflation, according to new data released on Friday.</p><p>Economists had said the labor market has been stuck in a “low-hire, low-fire” state, in which job growth is sluggish but layoffs also remain low, but October’s data surpassed economist expectations.       <title>Rural voters were feeling left behind before the midterms, poll shows</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/05/former-trump-voters-economy</link>
      <description><p>Polling done for the Guardian shows plummeting support from a former key constituency of Donald Trump’s base</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/community/live/2026/nov/05/what-happens-after-the-blue-wave-our-reporters-answer-your-midterm-election-results-questions">Q&amp;A: Ask your questions about Democrats’ win in the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>Polling conducted by the Harris Poll for the Guardian before the election shows just how angry voters were and points to one key reason Republicans lost so badly: plummeting support from rural voters, once a key constituency of Donald Trump’s base.</p><p>Over the summer, 95% of Americans indicated they believed there was an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/jul/07/cost-of-living-poll-groceries-gas">affordability crisis</a>, particularly because of steep gas and grocery prices. By October, 61% of voters <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/15/voters-economy-cost-of-living-prices-poll">believed</a> the country was experiencing a recession, even though technically it wasn’t.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/05/former-trump-voters-economy">Continue reading...</a></description>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/business/useconomy">US economy</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-administration">Trump administration</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/democrats">Democrats</category>

      <description><p>There’s not much they can do over the next couple of years to alleviate angry voters’ stress over prices</p><p>It was the economy, again.       <description><p>A layoff and a leap of faith convinced Katie Teixeira she had what it takes to run her own business</p><p>In 2010, Katie Teixeira adopted a kitten found all alone in an abandoned house. À l’occasion du 11-Novembre, France 24 vous raconte l’histoire de Samuel Gunsberg, imprimeur né à Budapest et installé en France en l'an 1900, interné dès 1914 comme "sujet ennemi". Son carnet inédit, retrouvé par son arrière-arrière-petite-fille, journaliste à France 24, lève le voile sur le sort méconnu des quelque 60 000 civils étrangers enfermés dans des camps en France pendant la Première Guerre mondiale.

La pétition pour "supprimer CNews de l'audiovisuel français" avait recueilli plus d’un million de signataires, autorisant sont débat à l'Assemblée nationale. Mardi, la commission des affaires culturelles et de l’éducation a cependant classé sans suite cette démarche par 28 votes contre 25.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5414cbc4-dd18-11f1-9de2-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6ZY3WE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5414cbc4-dd18-11f1-9de2-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6ZY3WE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">56d3b4a8-dd16-11f1-8337-431b6481e919</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:06:52 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5414cbc4-dd18-11f1-9de2-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6ZY3WE.jpg">© Simon Wohlfahrt, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Moyen-Orient</category><title>Israël en direct : le parti d'Eisenkot dépose un projet de loi pour créer une commission d'enquête sur le 7-Octobre</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/moyen-orient/20261110-en-direct-le-pr%C3%A9sident-isra%C3%A9lien-annonce-officiellement-l-investiture-du-nouveau-parlement</link><description>

Le parti d'Eisenkot a, pour sa part, déposé un projet de loi pour créer une commission d'enquête sur le 7-Octobre. Suivez notre live sur France 24.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1c592fa0-dd12-11f1-928c-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T141850Z-1559279949-RC22LOAXQNAM-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-POLITICS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1c592fa0-dd12-11f1-928c-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T141850Z-1559279949-RC22LOAXQNAM-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-POLITICS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1302e4e0-dd13-11f1-b2bc-f16223598ae6</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:29:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1c592fa0-dd12-11f1-928c-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T141850Z-1559279949-RC22LOAXQNAM-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-POLITICS.jpg">© Ronen Zvulun, Reuters</source><dc:creator>Aude MAZOUÉ</dc:creator></item><item><category>Asie-Pacifique</category><title>Ce que l’on sait sur les exercices de l’armée chinoise autour de Taïwan</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/asie-pacifique/20261110-ce-que-l-on-sait-sur-les-exercices-de-l-arm%C3%A9e-chinoise-autour-de-ta%C3%AFwan</link><description>
Depuis le début du mois de novembre, la Chine mène des exercices militaires majeurs autour de Taïwan. Mais contrairement à ce que laissent entendre des internautes, les forces armées chinoises n’ont pas instauré un blocus de l’île -  elles se livrent seulement à une simulation d’encerclement.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/92520268-dd08-11f1-8ebf-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/image3-138.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/92520268-dd08-11f1-8ebf-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/image3-138.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ba4b4f18-dd08-11f1-a7a3-47af395fef37</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:02:50 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/92520268-dd08-11f1-8ebf-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/image3-138.jpg">©  X, Institute for the Study of War.</source><dc:creator>Les Observateurs</dc:creator></item><item><category>Amériques</category><title>Procédure de destitution aux États-Unis : Pete Hegseth fustige une "mise en scène politique"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/am%C3%A9riques/20261110-%C3%A9tats-unis-proc%C3%A9dure-destitution-pete-hegseth-fustige-mise-en-sc%C3%A8ne-politique</link><description>
Lors d'une conférence de presse, le ministre américain de la Défense Pete Hegseth a qualifié mardi de "farce" et de "mise en scène politique" la procédure de destitution initiée à son encontre pour sa gestion de la guerre contre l'Iran.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/52a6cec0-dcf2-11f1-b362-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-06T012421Z-163758692-RC20IOALR7O5-RTRMADP-3-USA-TRUMP-HEGSETH.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/52a6cec0-dcf2-11f1-b362-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-06T012421Z-163758692-RC20IOALR7O5-RTRMADP-3-USA-TRUMP-HEGSETH.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3cb87578-dd0b-11f1-b2a3-1b978980c39d</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:44:15 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/52a6cec0-dcf2-11f1-b362-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-06T012421Z-163758692-RC20IOALR7O5-RTRMADP-3-USA-TRUMP-HEGSETH.jpg">via REUTERS - SECRETARY OF DEFENSE PETE HEGSET</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Les ministres du G7 réunis à Paris : l'Iran et l'Ukraine au cœur des débats</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261110-les-ministres-du-g7-r%C3%A9unis-%C3%A0-paris-l-iran-et-l-ukraine-au-c%C5%93ur-des-d%C3%A9bats</link><description>
Le chef de la diplomatie française, Jean-Noël Barrot, s'est entretenu mardi 10 novembre à Paris avec son homologue ukrainien, Andrii Sybiha, en marge de ⁠la réunion des ministres des Affaires étrangères du G7. Réunion au cours de laquelle la guerre en Ukraine et celle en Iran seront les sujets principaux entre les différents ministres. Les précisions de Pascale Joannin, directrice Générale de la Fondation Robert Schuman et de Karim Yahiaoui, journaliste à France 24.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c3519bbc-dd03-11f1-961c-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261110-130321-132542-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c3519bbc-dd03-11f1-961c-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261110-130321-132542-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c86ca51a-dd03-11f1-b014-2f6224affb59</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:39:42 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Parlons-en, les invités</category><title>Centres de données : le coup de chaud ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/parlons-en-les-invit%C3%A9s/20261110-centres-de-donn%C3%A9es-le-coup-de-chaud</link><description>
La colère gronde contre les centres de données. Depuis plusieurs mois, des États-Unis à l’Europe, des associations se mobilisent contre l’implantation de data centers. Énergivores, consommateurs d’eau, ils sont de plus en plus pointés du doigt, alors que leur déploiement est dopé par la progression de l’IA. Et les retombées économiques sur les territoires ne s'avèrent pas forcement à la hauteur des attentes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ad0b65ce-dcf7-11f1-8052-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FRAN261110-1000-Live-CS1000.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ad0b65ce-dcf7-11f1-8052-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/FRAN261110-1000-Live-CS1000.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5ef5d29c-dd07-11f1-82c1-3f605b48c77b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:31:12 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Faiza YOUNSI</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Mobilisations en France : une revalorisation qu'il "ne faut pas mépriser" (Lecornu)</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261110-mobilisations-en-france-une-revalorisation-qu-il-ne-faut-pas-m%C3%A9priser</link><description>

Le Premier ministre a annoncé en conférence de presse qu'il était important "de ne pas mépriser" cette hausse.
